question: What shortcomings in current agent benchmarks and evaluation practice make agents look better than they are or hinder real-world usefulness?
hypothesis: Accuracy-only, cost-blind benchmarking without holdouts or standardisation leads to needlessly complex agents and mistaken conclusions about what drives gains.
contributions: AI agent evaluations must be cost-controlled (Sec 2)
Jointly optimizing accuracy and cost yields better agent design (Sec 3)
Model and downstream developers have distinct benchmarking needs (Sec 4)
Agent benchmarks enable shortcuts; holdouts by generality level (Sec 5)
Agent evaluations lack standardization and reproducibility (Sec 6)

method.summary: Re-evaluates HumanEval agents (LDB, LATS, Reflexion) against simple retry, warming and escalation baselines on accuracy and dollar cost; adds Optuna-based joint cost-accuracy optimisation to DSPy on HotPotQA; case-studies NovelQA, WebArena and a 17-benchmark holdout survey.
method.task: Agent evaluation methodology (code generation, multi-hop QA, long-document QA, web tasks)

datasets.name: HumanEval (LDB-modified, example tests for all 164 tasks)
HotPotQA
datasets.size: 100 train samples for optimisation (50/50 candidate/validation for random search and joint), 200 eval samples
datasets.source: Yang et al.; Wikipedia 2017 dump via ColBERTv2

inference.decoding: Retry: temperature 0, up to 5 trials until example tests pass. Warming: temperature 0 first trial, 0.3 for trials 2-3, 0.5 for trials 4-5. Escalation: llama-3-8b-chat-hf, gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, llama-3-70b-chat-hf, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 in order, temperature 0
inference.temperature: see decoding; LDB 0; LATS 0.8 generation, 0.2 reflections/tests; Reflexion 0 generation, 0.2 tests/reflections
inference.samples: 5 runs per agent on HumanEval and HotPotQA, mean reported with min/max; NovelQA single run
inference.prompting: Zero-shot LDB prompt plus example tests; NovelQA original prompt with retrieved snippets
inference.retrieval: HotPotQA: ColBERTv2, 2 hops, 2 passages. NovelQA RAG: 10 chunks of 1000 characters, text-embedding-3-large

parameters.LATS: max iterations 8, expansion factor 3, max internal tests 6 (GPT-3.5) or 4 (GPT-4)
parameters.DSPy: max 8 demonstrations, random search 16 candidate programs
parameters.Optuna: 16 trials; module temperatures from 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6; searched temperature, number of few-shot examples, example selection, formatting instructions

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: HumanEval: solution passes the true tests; HotPotQA: all ground-truth documents retrieved; NovelQA: multiple-choice accuracy

metrics.name: Total cost
metrics.definition: Dollar cost of API calls at stated provider prices; HotPotQA splits variable cost (per 100 inferences) and fixed optimisation cost

eval.protocol: Pareto frontier constrained convex; 95% CIs by Student's t over 5 runs (HotPotQA); min/max across runs elsewhere

prompts.text: You are a literature professor. I will provide you with snippets from a novel along with a question and corresponding choices pertaining to it. Please thoroughly analyze the content to accurately respond to the question. Relevant snippets from the novel: <context> Question: <question> Only respond with the index of the correct answer (e.g., choose between A, B, C, and D). Your output should not contain anything else.

results.note: Table A3: joint optimization 0.509 acc, variable cost 0.174 vs 0.376 (random search) and 0.384 (few-shot) per 100 inferences

results.quote: 7/17 benchmarks do not include holdout sets for evaluating agents’ performance and do not indicate plans to do so

results.claim: Appropriate holdouts by generality level: 1/1 distribution-specific, 3/6 task-specific, 1/8 domain-general, 0/2 fully general

limits: Cost models change with provider pricing; mitigated by a web app for repricing
Does not cover all task environments or agent types; programming and one QA benchmark carry the empirical weight
Environmental, annotation-labour and maintenance costs not analysed
System 2 approaches may still help on harder tasks such as SWE-bench
NovelQA run once, no error bars
Joint optimisation is a simple starting point; error bars exclude optimisation variability
Generality level of each benchmark was the authors' best guess
